title: Acute dystonia from antipsychotics: D2 receptor antagonism
vignette: A 22-year-old man comes to the emergency department due to sudden-onset pain and stiffness on one side of his neck. He was diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder 2 days ago and has been adherent with his newly prescribed medication. For the past few months, the patient has heard voices telling him to quit his job, and he believes that his girlfriend's parents are monitoring his sexual thoughts with a special device. He has been socially withdrawn and has difficulty showering regularly. Vital signs are within normal limits. The head is tilted to one side and cannot be straightened without considerable pain. The most likely cause of this patient's symptoms is antagonism of which of the following receptors?

clues.text: diagnosed with a psychiatric disorder 2 days ago and has been adherent with his newly prescribed medication
clues.note: Recent initiation of a newly prescribed medication (an antipsychotic) is the key setup - acute dystonia develops within hours to days of starting.

clues.text: heard voices telling him to quit his job
clues.note: Auditory hallucinations plus delusions and negative symptoms indicate schizophrenia, treated with dopamine (D2)-blocking antipsychotics.

clues.text: head is tilted to one side and cannot be straightened without considerable pain
clues.note: Painful, sustained muscle contraction pulling the head to one side is acute dystonia (spasmodic torticollis) - an extrapyramidal side effect of D2 blockade.

whatMatters: A patient just started on an antipsychotic for schizophrenia who develops acute painful torticollis has an ACUTE DYSTONIC REACTION - an extrapyramidal symptom from DOPAMINE D2 RECEPTOR ANTAGONISM in the nigrostriatal pathway. Answer B. (Treat with an anticholinergic such as benztropine or the antihistamine diphenhydramine.)
strategy: Recognize acute dystonia (sudden sustained muscle spasm/torticollis, 4 hours-4 days after starting an antipsychotic) and attribute it to D2 blockade in the nigrostriatal pathway, which unbalances dopamine vs cholinergic tone -> extrapyramidal symptoms. Reject the receptors that explain OTHER antipsychotic side effects: alpha-1 (orthostatic hypotension), H1 (sedation/weight gain), M1 (anticholinergic - dry mouth/constipation), 5-HT2A (blocked by atypicals but doesn't cause dystonia), and GABA-A (flumazenil/benzodiazepines).

eliminations.label: Alpha-1 adrenergic - orthostatic hypotension
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: alpha-1 blockade by antipsychotics. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes orthostatic hypotension/dizziness, not dystonia. ✅ Correct if: postural hypotension on a low-potency antipsychotic.

eliminations.label: GABA-A - benzodiazepines/flumazenil
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: the benzodiazepine-modulated chloride channel. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: GABA-A is not the antipsychotic target causing dystonia. ✅ Correct if: benzodiazepine effect or flumazenil reversal.

eliminations.label: Histaminergic H1 - sedation/weight gain
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: H1 blockade. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes sedation and weight gain, not extrapyramidal dystonia. ✅ Correct if: sedation/weight gain from an antipsychotic or antihistamine.

eliminations.label: Muscarinic M1 - anticholinergic effects
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: muscarinic blockade. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it causes dry mouth, constipation, urinary retention, blurred vision - and MORE M1 blockade actually LESSENS extrapyramidal symptoms (low-potency antipsychotics cause fewer EPS). ✅ Correct if: anticholinergic side effects.

eliminations.label: Serotonergic 5-HT2A - atypical mechanism, not dystonia (your pick)
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: 5-HT2A antagonism, prominent in SECOND-generation (atypical) antipsychotics. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: 5-HT2A blockade actually helps REDUCE extrapyramidal symptoms (fewer EPS with atypicals); it does not CAUSE acute dystonia - that's D2 blockade. ✅ Correct if: explaining why atypicals have fewer EPS.

reasoning: Schizophrenia + newly started antipsychotic + acute painful torticollis = acute dystonic reaction
Acute dystonia is an extrapyramidal symptom from dopamine D2 receptor blockade in the nigrostriatal pathway
D2 blockade unbalances dopaminergic/cholinergic tone in the striatum -> excess cholinergic activity
mechanism: Antipsychotics treat schizophrenia primarily by blocking dopamine D2 receptors in the mesolimbic pathway. However, D2 blockade in the NIGROSTRIATAL pathway causes EXTRAPYRAMIDAL SYMPTOMS (EPS). In the striatum, inhibitory dopamine (D2) tone is normally balanced by excitatory cholinergic (M1) neurons; strong D2 blockade unmasks a relative CHOLINERGIC EXCESS, producing movement side effects. ACUTE DYSTONIA - sudden, sustained, often painful muscle contractions such as spasmodic TORTICOLLIS, oculogyric crisis, or (rarely) laryngospasm - can develop abruptly, typically 4 hours to 4 days after starting the drug, and is most common with HIGH-POTENCY first-generation agents (e.g., haloperidol, fluphenazine). It is treated by restoring the dopamine-acetylcholine balance with an ANTICHOLINERGIC (benztropine) or the antihistamine diphenhydramine. The other EPS (akathisia, parkinsonism, and later tardive dyskinesia) also stem from D2 blockade. The distractor receptors explain different antipsychotic effects (alpha-1 -> orthostasis, H1 -> sedation, M1 -> anticholinergic and FEWER EPS, 5-HT2A -> fewer EPS with atypicals); GABA-A is unrelated.

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Psych/Pharm > antipsychotic EPS: D2 blockade (nigrostriatal) -> acute dystonia (hours-days), akathisia, parkinsonism, tardive dyskinesia; treat acute dystonia with benztropine/diphenhydramine; high-potency agents worst.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Acute torticollis days after a new antipsychotic = D2-blockade extrapyramidal reaction.

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on acute dystonia/torticollis, extrapyramidal symptoms, nigrostriatal pathway, or D2 vs 5-HT2A? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Alpha-1 (orthostasis), H1 (sedation), M1 (anticholinergic, fewer EPS), 5-HT2A (fewer EPS with atypicals), GABA-A (benzodiazepines) don't cause dystonia.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: acute dystonia = D2 blockade (nigrostriatal); treat benztropine/diphenhydramine; high-potency antipsychotics highest risk.

keywords.front: Acute torticollis days after starting an antipsychotic

firstAid.detail: Pharm: D2 blockade (nigrostriatal) -> extrapyramidal dystonia; treat benztropine/diphenhydramine.
Psych > high-potency (haloperidol) -> more EPS; low-potency -> more anticholinergic/sedation.

memoryHook: Block D2 in the motor striatum and acetylcholine runs wild - the neck cramps into torticollis days after the first antipsychotic dose; benztropine rebalances it.
